paras: The mob assault on Mr. Love was an attack in or near Somerset, Kentucky, reported in January 1881, in which a mob led by Love's wife chased him and left him hanging head downward from a tree. Love survived after a preacher cut him down about two hours later, almost frozen. The episode is known only from a short, unsigned paragraph that white newspapers in at least ten states reprinted as a curiosity about how Somerset treated "faithless husbands."

The paragraph gives no date, first name or race for Love, and says only that "public opinion on the subject of faithless husbands is very strong in Somerset, Ky." and that Love "was that kind of an offender." It does not say what he was alleged to have done beyond that phrase.

According to the item, Love's wife led a mob against him, and he fled "without coat, trousers or boots" with the crowd close behind. After about a mile the pursuers caught him and left him "suspended, head downward, from a tree." Two hours later a preacher, described as "humane," cut him down; by then he was "almost frozen to death."
No report of arrests, charges or any official response appears in the coverage, and no local Kentucky account was found.

The story circulated as filler rather than news: the identical paragraph, with no dateline or credited source, appeared in the Southern Standard of McMinnville, Tennessee, on January 22, 1881, and in the Iron County Register of Ironton, Missouri, and the Fayette County Herald of Ohio on January 27. Through February and March it ran in papers in Maryland, Louisiana, Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota and Tennessee, often beside unrelated miscellany such as a feature on Leadville or sardine exports. The Independent Statesman of New Hampshire carried a shorter rewrite on February 17 that dropped Love's name, said he was "tied head downward to a tree," and had the preacher find him "just in time to save his life." The Cheyenne Daily Leader printed it as late as June 26, 1881.

Its tone was wry, opening with a remark on Somerset's "public opinion" and closing on the preacher's rescue, and no paper added comment on the mob. The Cheyenne paper ran it under the heading "News Brevities" among oddities from Nevada, Pennsylvania and England.
